title: Signs of the end (Matthew 24:1–31)
hookLine: wars and rumors on every screen, and a first instruction that isn't a date
tomorrow: nobody knows the hour. so what are you meant to be doing?
last: HOW OFTEN I WOULD HAVE GATHERED YOU.

lines: EVERY SCREEN FEELS LIKE AN ENDING.
cards: Breaking news, a siren in the background, a video from someone's phone. Some weeks every screen feels like an ending. Leaving the Temple, the disciples point out its buildings, the way people point at a skyline.

Jesus answers: "There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down." Later, on the Mount of Olives, they come to him privately with the question people still ask in frightening times.
When will these things be? And what will be the sign of his coming, and of the end of the world? Two questions in one breath, the stones and the end, and Christians still read his answer in two ways.

teach.b: His first words aren't a date. "Take heed that no man deceive you." Then: "ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet."
Famines, earthquakes, nation against nation: "All these are the beginning of sorrows." The love of many will grow cold. "But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved."
So what is this chapter about? Christians answer two ways, and each has a real case.
Some read much of it as the Temple's fall. Their case: Jesus starts with those very stones, and later says, "This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled."
The Temple did fall to Rome later, they point out, just as he said.

teach.h: READING TWO: AN END STILL AHEAD.
teach.b: Others hear a future end, still ahead. Their case: the sun darkened, the Son of man coming on the clouds with power, angels gathering his elect from the four winds.
That hasn't happened yet, they say, and it's too large for one city. Some hold a bit of both.
Here's what both sides share: the first instructions. Don't be fooled.
Don't be troubled. Keep loving while love cools around you. The rumors will keep coming either way.

how: Christians read Matthew 24 in different ways, as the Temple's fall, a future return of Christ, or both; the Nicene Creed, said in the worship of a number of churches, says Christ shall come again with glory.

games.q: what does “signs of the end” mean?
o: a list of omens that reveals the exact final date
Jesus' words on the Temple's fall and the end of the age
the comets and eclipses seen when Jesus was born

games.q: signs of the end — tap the pairs.
p: what he says of the Temple
see that ye be not troubled
a verse the Temple reading leans on

s: in Matthew 24, Jesus gives the disciples a date for the end
his first words are a warning, take heed that no man deceive you, and he says the end is not yet.
wars and earthquakes mean the end has arrived
"all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet... the beginning of sorrows."
Christians read this chapter in more than one way
some as the Temple's fall, some as a future end, some as a bit of both.

games.q: you read Matthew 24 as all about a future end. a friend reads it as the Temple's fall, long ago. what's the strongest case for your friend's side?
o: it starts with the Temple's stones, and says this generation shall not pass.
nobody back then cared much what happened to the Temple.
the chapter never mentions anything that could be future.
games.why: the Temple reading leans on 24:2 and 24:34. the future reading leans on the Son of man on the clouds (24:30). both keep the first instruction: be not troubled.

practice: Find one steady sound near you: a fan, rain, traffic, a refrigerator's hum, your own breath. For this sit, let that one sound be louder than any headline.
When the news drifts back in, return to the sound, and let the three words ride on it: be not troubled.

wordCard.voice: Signs of the end. Jesus' words about the Temple and the end of the age, which open with a warning to stay calm.

orig.note: Greek for age: the disciples ask about the end of the age, 'end of the world' in the KJV (Matthew 24:3).

carryVoice: Hold onto this: be not troubled, because the end, he says, is not yet. Peace for today.
